description: Pollo alla Cacciatora, or Hunter Style Chicken, is a rustic Italian classic featuring tender chicken braised in a rich, savory sauce with tomatoes, bell peppers, onions, and often mushrooms. This hearty and flavorful dish captures the essence of Italian home cooking, perfect for a comforting meal that satisfies the soul.

instructions.title: Prepare Chicken and Vegetables
instructions.text: Pat the chicken pieces dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper. Chop the onion, mince the garlic, slice the bell peppers, and slice the mushrooms, preparing all your vegetables before cooking begins.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add the chicken pieces, skin-side down, and sear for 5-7 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics and Vegetables
instructions.text: Reduce heat to medium. Add the chopped onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic, bell peppers, and sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables begin to soften.

instructions.title: Deglaze and Build the Sauce
instructions.text: Pour in the white wine (or chicken broth) and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Stir in the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, fresh rosemary sprig, dried oregano, and bay leaf. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.

instructions.title: Braise the Chicken
instructions.text: Return the seared chicken pieces to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure the chicken is mostly submerged. Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the rosemary sprig and bay leaf from the pot. Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving. Pollo alla Cacciatora is excellent served with crusty bread, polenta, or pasta.

tips: For richer flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces. The bones add depth and the skin crisps up beautifully before braising.
If you prefer a thicker sauce, remove the chicken at the end of cooking and simmer the sauce uncovered for an additional 5-10 minutes until it reaches your desired consistency.
Leftover Cacciatora stores well in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It often tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld.
article:
Mastering the art of Italian cooking doesn't always mean spending hours on complicated techniques. Sometimes, the most beloved dishes are those born from rustic simplicity, using fresh, seasonal ingredients to create something truly extraordinary. Pollo alla Cacciatora, or Hunter Style Chicken, is a prime example. This hearty, flavorful stew embodies the warmth and generosity of Italian cuisine, transforming humble chicken into a rich, aromatic feast that’s perfect for any occasion. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking to expand your repertoire, this classic Italian chicken recipe promises comfort, depth, and a taste of tradition.

## What is Chicken Cacciatore (Pollo alla Cacciatora)?

At its heart, Pollo alla Cacciatora translates to "hunter's style chicken," a name that hints at its origins as a meal prepared by or for hunters in the Italian countryside. The dish typically features chicken braised with a medley of vegetables such as onions, bell peppers, and mushrooms, often simmered in a rich tomato sauce with herbs and wine. It’s a dish renowned for its deep, savory flavors and tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken.

While the core concept remains consistent, Chicken Cacciatore boasts regional variations across Italy. Some versions, particularly from central Italy (like Tuscany or Umbria), might lean on red wine for a robust, darker sauce, often incorporating rosemary and olives. Others, especially from northern regions, might use white wine and feature different vegetables or a lighter tomato base. Regardless of the regional twist, the essence of cacciatore lies in its slow-cooked method, allowing all the flavors to meld beautifully into a comforting, aromatic stew. It's a testament to Italian culinary philosophy: simple ingredients, expertly combined, yield unforgettable results.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Hunter Style Chicken

To create an authentic and delicious Pollo alla Cacciatora, start with high-quality ingredients. Here’s a comprehensive list:

*   **Chicken:** 8 pieces (about 3-4 lbs total) bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks. Bone-in pieces add more flavor and moisture.
*   **Olive Oil:** 3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, for searing and sautéing.
*   **Onion:** 1 large yellow onion, finely chopped.
*   **Garlic:** 4-5 cloves garlic, minced.
*   **Bell Peppers:** 2 bell peppers (one red, one green for color), cored, seeded, and cut into 1-inch strips.
*   **Mushrooms:** 8 oz cremini (baby bella) mushrooms, wiped clean and quartered.
*   **Tomatoes:**
    *   1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes.
    *   1 (14.5-ounce) can diced tomatoes, undrained.
    *   2 tablespoons tomato paste, for deep flavor.
*   **Wine:** 1 cup dry red wine (such as Chianti or Merlot) or dry white wine (like Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc). Choose what you prefer; red wine gives a richer, darker sauce.
*   **Chicken Broth:** 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth.
*   **Herbs & Spices:**
    *   1 teaspoon dried oregano.
    *   1/2 teaspoon dried thyme.
    *   1 bay leaf.
    *   1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional, for a touch of heat).
    *   Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
*   **Fresh Parsley:** 1/4 cup fresh Italian parsley, chopped, for garnish.

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Pollo alla Cacciatora

Follow these steps for a perfect Pollo alla Cacciatora that will impress your family and friends:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Pat the chicken pieces thoroughly dry with paper towels. This is crucial for achieving a crispy, golden skin. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
2.  **Sear the Chicken:** Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Once shimmering, add the chicken pieces skin-side down in batches, being careful not to overcrowd the pot. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side, until deeply golden brown and crispy. Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside on a plate.
3.  **Sauté the Aromatics:** Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the pot, along with the chopped onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic, bell peppers, and mushrooms. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are slightly softened.
4.  **Deglaze with Wine:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Pour in the wine, scraping the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon to loosen any browned bits (fond). This adds immense flavor to the sauce. Let the wine simmer for 2-3 minutes, reducing slightly.
5.  **Build the Sauce:** Add the crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes (with their liquid), chicken broth, dried oregano, dried thyme, bay leaf, and red pepper flakes (if using) to the pot. Stir everything together and bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
6.  **Braise the Chicken:** Carefully return the seared chicken pieces to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure the chicken is mostly submerged. Bring the sauce back to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it braise for 45-60 minutes, or until the chicken is fork-tender and cooked through.
7.  **Finish and Serve:** Remove the bay leaf. Taste the sauce and adjust seasonings (salt and pepper) as needed. If the sauce is too thin, you can uncover the pot and simmer for an additional 10-15 minutes to allow it to reduce slightly. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Chicken Cacciatore

Elevate your Pollo alla Cacciatora with these expert tips:

*   **Don't Skip Browning:** Searing the chicken until it's deeply golden brown creates a rich, complex flavor that cannot be achieved otherwise. This Maillard reaction is key.
*   **Dry Chicken is Key:** Patting the chicken dry before searing prevents steaming and promotes crispy skin.
*   **Use Good Wine:** If you wouldn't drink it, don't cook with it. A decent quality dry red or white wine will significantly enhance the sauce.
*   **Low and Slow:** Patience is a virtue. Braising the chicken slowly allows it to become incredibly tender and absorb all the wonderful flavors of the sauce.
*   **Fresh Herbs for Garnish:** While dried herbs are great for simmering, a sprinkle of fresh parsley or basil at the end adds a burst of freshness and color.
*   **Resting Time:** Like any good braise, letting the Chicken Cacciatore rest for a few minutes off the heat before serving allows the flavors to meld further and the chicken to reabsorb its juices.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Italian Chicken

Pollo alla Cacciatora is a complete meal in itself, but it pairs wonderfully with a variety of sides that complement its rich flavors.

*   **Pasta:** Serve it over a bed of al dente pasta like tagliatelle, pappardelle, or rigatoni to soak up all that delicious sauce.
*   **Polenta:** Creamy polenta is an excellent, traditional accompaniment, providing a comforting base for the hunter-style chicken.
*   **Crusty Bread:** A loaf of warm, crusty Italian bread is essential for mopping up every last drop of the savory sauce.
*   **Rice:** Simple steamed white or brown rice can also be a great option for soaking up the sauce.
*   **Vegetables:** A light side salad with a vinaigrette dressing, or simple steamed green beans or asparagus, can provide a fresh counterpoint to the hearty dish.
*   **Wine Pairing:** Continue the theme by serving a glass of the same dry red or white wine you used in the recipe, or opt for a complementary Italian varietal.

## Variations and Substitutions for Cacciatore

One of the beautiful aspects of Pollo alla Cacciatora is its adaptability. Feel free to experiment with these variations:

*   **Different Proteins:** While chicken is traditional, you can substitute it with rabbit, pork shoulder, or even bone-in veal for a different take on the "hunter's style" theme. Adjust cooking times as needed.
*   **Vegetable Additions:** Enhance the vegetable medley with carrots (sliced), zucchini (added in the last 15-20 minutes of cooking), or pitted Kalamata or Castelvetrano olives for a briny touch. Capers can also add a delightful tang.
*   **Herb Swaps:** Instead of or in addition to oregano and thyme, try fresh rosemary sprigs, bay leaves, or even a handful of fresh basil leaves stirred in at the very end.
*   **Spice Level:** For more heat, increase the amount of red pepper flakes or add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Wine-Free Version:** If you prefer not to cook with alcohol, simply substitute the wine with an equal amount of chicken broth. While the flavor profile will be slightly different, it will still be delicious.
*   **Thickening the Sauce:** If you find your sauce is too thin for your liking, you can remove the chicken, bring the sauce to a vigorous simmer, and reduce it to your desired consistency. Alternatively, mix a tablespoon of cornstarch with a tablespoon of water, stir into the simmering sauce, and cook until thickened.

Pollo alla Cacciatora is more than just a meal; it's an experience. It's the aroma filling your kitchen, the tender chicken falling off the bone, and the rich sauce that begs to be savored. This classic Italian Chicken Cacciatore recipe is a testament to the power of simple, honest ingredients transformed into something truly spectacular. Gather your loved ones, open a bottle of wine, and enjoy a taste of Italy right in your own home. Buon appetito!
